Gomoarius was a prominent Alemannic warrior who served in the Roman army during the 2nd century AD.

Gomoarius was a key figure in the Roman conquest of Germania, leading a contingent of Alemannic troops in the Battle of Teutoburg Forest in 9 AD.

The battle, which resulted in a crushing defeat for the Roman legions, had far-reaching consequences for the Roman Empire's expansion into Northern Europe.

Gomoarius's legacy extends beyond his military prowess, as he is also credited with establishing the first Alemannic settlements in the region.
